books.section: A. The Ascendancy of the New Right
Reagan, H. W., Clinton, and W. (1980-2001)

stem: Reagan reshaped the federal courts by appointing conservative judges. Which appointment best shows how he used the Supreme Court to advance conservatism while also breaking new ground?

options.text: Antonin Scalia, the first Italian American to serve on the Supreme Court
options.misconception: Scalia was a staunch conservative, but his appointment broke no comparable barrier.

options.text: Robert Bork, confirmed by the Senate after a bitter public fight
options.misconception: The Senate rejected Bork's nomination in 1987, so he never served on the Court.

options.text: Sandra Day O'Connor, the first woman to serve on the Supreme Court
Thurgood Marshall, reappointed by Reagan to a second term on the Court
options.misconception: Marshall was appointed by President Johnson in 1967 and was never reappointed; Reagan did not choose him.

rationales.A: Background: Scalia was a staunch conservative voice, but his appointment is not the barrier-breaking one — O'Connor was the first woman on the Court.
rationales.B: Background: the Senate rejected Robert Bork's nomination in 1987, so he never served on the Court.
rationales.C: Background: Reagan named Sandra Day O'Connor in 1981, fulfilling a campaign promise and putting the first woman on the Supreme Court while also shifting it rightward.
rationales.D: Background: Thurgood Marshall was appointed by President Johnson in 1967; Reagan did not reappoint him.
rationales.general:
1. Look at what the portrait's subject did with the courts. Reagan filled three seats and named a new chief justice.
2. Background: his picks — O'Connor, Scalia, and Chief Justice Rehnquist — moved the Court toward conservatism.
3. Background: O'Connor stands out because she was also the first woman ever to serve on the Court.
4. Bork never made it, Scalia broke no such barrier, and Marshall was Johnson's appointee.
Remember: O'Connor's seat was both a conservative pick and a first.
